interview:
I did not win. Here's an honest account of what happened:

I successfully started the game by entering the name "Chonk" and pressing Play. The board loaded with Le Chonk (the orange cat) in the bottom-left area, the blue fish in the top-right corner, the guard dog in the middle, and several yellow X obstacle squares.

However, I then spent the entire session struggling to make valid moves. I repeatedly clicked on squares that were not adjacent to the cat — I misjudged the grid coordinates and kept clicking too far away, on the cat itself, or on cells that weren't valid one-square moves. Each time, the game displayed the message "Le Chonk can only move one square," indicating my clicks were rejected as invalid moves.

The cat barely moved from its starting position (it may have shifted one square at most, and the move counter showed "Moves: 3"), while the guard dog gradually closed in. The session ended with the cat still near the bottom-left of the board, nowhere close to the fish at the top-right, and the dog nearby. I never reached the fish, so I lost — or rather, never got anywhere at all.

The main problem was my poor aim with the click coordinates: I confused which cell was adjacent to the cat and clicked wrong cells dozens of times instead of calmly identifying the exact neighboring square and clicking its center.
